summary.headline: KPI Green Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to Rs 741 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 92 crore from Rs 117 crore on higher IPP depreciation and finance costs.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 total income of Rs 741 crore (up 16% YoY from Rs 641 crore) and EBITDA of Rs 283 crore (up 22% YoY from Rs 232 crore), with EBITDA margin at 38%. Profit after tax fell to Rs 92 crore from Rs 117 crore, which management attributed to higher depreciation and finance cost from IPP asset commissioning. H1 FY27 totals were total income Rs 1,451 crore, EBITDA Rs 545 crore, PAT Rs 187 crore and cash profit Rs 355 crore. Management guided FY27 PAT of about Rs 500 crore, with a binding agreement to acquire 507.9 MW of operating Gujarat wind assets for an enterprise value of about Rs 240 crore.

financial_highlights.change: +16% YoY vs Rs 641 crore in Q2 FY26
vs Rs 117 crore in Q2 FY26 (decline)

segments.name: IPP (independent power producer)
segments.commentary: Installed IPP capacity expected to reach about 2.1 GW by March 2027, up from negligible about four years ago. H1 FY27 additions: 317 MW hybrid IPP project (cumulative 511 MW) and 50 MW of a 350 MW solar IPP project (cumulative 301 MW).

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Commissioned 269 MW solar for Coal India's Khavda project and 128 MW solar for Mahagenco in Maharashtra. Secured an IPP order of about Rs 2,000 crore for a 500 MW solar project for NACoP Purja Pvt Ltd in Rajasthan.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Pipeline of 565 MW, with 1,130 MWh for which BESS purchase agreements have been executed. Integrated storage campus under development in Gujarat, starting with assembly and moving to cell manufacturing later.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of about Rs 500 crore, with management saying it could be exceeded because H2 has historically been stronger than H1.
Long-term target of 25% YoY growth, reiterated from the KPI 3.0 event.
Acquisition of Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind (100% each, EV about Rs 240 crore) expected to close by March 2027. Management expects 350-400 crore of revenue from the 507.9 MW wind assets.
Installed IPP capacity expected to reach about 2.1 GW by end-March 2027.
Sun Drop Energy (BESS manufacturing) targeted to list in 18-24 months, with pre-IPO rounds in progress. Management also gave a shorter 'under 18 months' timeline in response to a question.
FY28 guidance to be given in Q4 FY27 results, per a response on the call.
capex_capacity: Total renewable portfolio about 8.33 GW: 3.02 GW installed and 5.3 GW under execution. Split: 3.22 GW IPP and 5.11 GW EPC.
Land bank of 88.07 acres and evacuation capacity access of about 5.2 GW.

Sufficient equity to be raised to complete BESS manufacturing and IPP projects; financial closure already achieved for some BESS IPP projects, with equity from the promoter and pre-IPO rounds at Sun Drop.
Wind assets acquired at about Rs 2,400 crore, versus an estimated replacement cost of Rs 3,750-4,000 crore (about Rs 7.5-8 crore per MW).
demand_pricing: Management cites India's over 300 GW non-fossil capacity and 500 GW 2030 target, with growth shifting toward hybrid, RTC/FDRE, BESS, floating solar and C&I solutions.
Management said there is no listed Indian player better than KPI for wind EPC. Future wind EPC work for its own IPP projects will go to the EPC arm, with no reverse inter-company solar orders.
Management said the stock is not being valued fairly, citing a sector-wide de-rating in renewables over the past two to two and a half years.

qa_highlights.question: Shareholder questioned the promoter royalty (2% of revenue) and the capping, and whether shareholders voted on the capping.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the royalty was approved by shareholders, with about 75% of non-promoter shareholders voting in favour and the promoter abstaining. The promoter can reduce the royalty by informing the board; the board has not yet taken this up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock valued below peers, given the IPP business's recurring cash profits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can only execute well and that the market will value the company correctly over time. It agreed sector valuations are around Rs 8-10 crore per MW and said Alfanar/Netra closing could slip by about 15 days but will be done by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider demerging the IPP business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a demerger needs enough scale first, and it would take time once the IPP base is built to around 2.1 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 profit expectation and will wind orders go to the EPC arm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about Rs 500 crore PAT for FY27, possibly higher. Future wind EPC orders from KPI IPP projects will go to KPI Energy EPC; no solar cross-orders will be placed.

qa_highlights.question: How will funding for BESS manufacturing and IPP build-out be raised, and what is the Sun Drop listing timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited sufficient equity, promoter infusion and pre-IPO rounds at Sun Drop, with listing targeted within 18 to 24 months (later stated as under 18 months).

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential from the recently acquired 507.9 MW wind assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 350-400 crore of revenue from the wind assets, citing cost-recovery opportunity in Gujarat because of previously unresolved issues with the existing developer.

risks_watch: Higher depreciation and finance cost from IPP commissioning compressed Q2 PAT (down to Rs 92 crore from Rs 117 crore YoY) until IPP revenue stabilises.
Related-party royalty paid to the promoter (about 2% of revenue, now with a cap). Management did not confirm when the cap will be taken to the board; a shareholder raised governance concerns.
Execution risk on 5.3 GW under execution and on the 2.1 GW IPP target by March 2027. The 2,000 crore order for 500 MW Rajasthan solar is also new.
Completion of the Alfanar and Netra acquisition by March 2027 and the 350-400 crore revenue target from the acquired wind assets.
Sun Drop pre-IPO and listing timeline, which management has given inconsistently (18-24 months, then under 18 months).
Change of statutory auditor to BDO from the current quarter; the transition is not yet tested over a full reporting cycle.
Management sought to explain the valuation gap but gave no concrete plan for it, and the Q&A was muffled and partly unclear in the transcript.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the IPP build-out, but defensive and evasive on valuation, royalty and demerger questions, which it deflected to market behaviour and future work.
key_quotes: So what we can assure you is that we are on a path to long term sustainable growth of 25% year on year which we have given as a target in our KB 3.0 event as well as the presentation which is on the website.
As of now I can guide you for about 500 crores we can hope to surpass that and achieve more because generally as I have a h2 has been much better than h1 in past also

adds.what: IPP capacity to reach about 2.1 GW by March 2027 (H1 FY27 additions: 317 MW hybrid IPP project, cumulative 511 MW; 50 MW of 350 MW solar IPP project, cumulative
Acquired 507.9 MW operating Gujarat wind assets (Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind), EV about Rs 240 crore, expected to close by March 2027
BESS integrated storage campus in Gujarat, starting with assembly and moving to cell manufacturing later

growth.why: Management guides FY27 PAT of about Rs 500 crore (could be exceeded) and a long-term 25% YoY growth target, backed by IPP capacity reaching about 2.1 GW by March 2027, a Rs 5,700 crore order book and the 507.9 MW wind acquisition expected to add Rs 350-400 crore revenue; specific timing and capex for most additions is partly given, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin was 38% (EBITDA Rs 283 crore on Rs 741 crore income), but PAT fell to Rs 92 crore from Rs 117 crore as IPP depreciation and finance costs rose, and no explicit margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: IPP capacity is under construction to reach about 2.1 GW by March 2027 (cumulative 511 MW hybrid and 301 MW solar in H1), with 5.3 GW under execution.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IPP capacity is ramping toward 2.1 GW by March 2027 from 3.02 GW installed, and the 507.9 MW acquired wind assets are expected to add Rs 350-400 crore of revenue; the Rs 5,700 crore order book supports this.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said sufficient equity will be raised for BESS manufacturing and IPP projects, with the Gujarat storage campus planned and financial closure achieved on some BESS IPP projects; utilisation is not disclosed, so the case rests on the stated build-out plan rather than a utilisation level.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 PAT of about Rs 500 crore and said it could be surpassed because H2 has historically been stronger than H1; H1 PAT was Rs 187 crore, so H2 needs about Rs 313 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk on 5.3 GW under execution and the 2.1 GW IPP target, rising depreciation and finance costs, and the Alfanar/Netra close could slip about 15 days, although management expects completion by March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The BESS integrated campus in Gujarat starts with assembly and moves to cell manufacturing later, with the campus planned for Q4 FY27 and no commercial launch date given.

rows.label: Rs 2,000 crore 500 MW Rajasthan solar IPP order (NACoP Purja)
rows.why: The order is secured and adds to the Rs 5,700 crore order book, though execution timing was not disclosed.

rows.label: Sun Drop Energy pre-IPO and listing
rows.why: Pre-IPO rounds are in progress, but the timeline was given inconsistently (18-24 months, then under 18 months), so a listing inside the 2-4 quarter window is unlikely.

rows.label: Acquisition of Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind (507.9 MW)
rows.why: The binding agreement is in place at about Rs 240 crore EV, with management saying closing could slip about 15 days but will be done by March 2027, and 350-400 crore of revenue is expected.

tone.note: Management was confident on the IPP build-out to 2.1 GW, the Rs 500 crore PAT guide and the wind acquisition, but was defensive and evasive on valuation, the promoter royalty and demerger questions, which it deflected to market behaviour.
